citation_status: sources[] are archives to verify against, not yet cited page by page. Every entry needs object- or page-level citations before launch.

milestones.title: Bone needles in the Altai
milestones.blurb: Among the oldest known needles, implying sewn, fitted clothing.
milestones.context: Needles from Denisova Cave (Siberia) are dated only approximately. The clothing itself has not survived; sewn garments are an inference.

milestones.title: Twisted and dyed flax fibres
milestones.blurb: Early evidence of spun, coloured plant fibre.
milestones.context: Flax fibres from Dzudzuana Cave in Georgia include twisted and dyed examples. Their use in clothing is interpretation.

milestones.title: The Tarkhan dress
milestones.blurb: A pleated linen garment, among the oldest woven dress known.
milestones.context: Found at Tarkhan, Egypt, and now in the Petrie Museum, London. A radiocarbon range, not a single year.

milestones.title: New Kingdom linen, pleating and wigs
milestones.blurb: Fine pleated linen, broad collars, wigs and heavy jewellery.
milestones.context: Tomb painting, relief, statuary and surviving textiles (including the Tutankhamun burial) show elite dress. Dates follow the conventional chronology.

milestones.title: Paracas and Nasca textiles
milestones.blurb: Embroidered mantles and tunics from the Peruvian coast.
milestones.context: Preserved in dry burials. Dates are broad ranges for two overlapping cultures.

milestones.title: Ottoman court caftans
milestones.blurb: Silk and metal-thread caftans signalled rank at the Ottoman court.
milestones.context: Large surviving groups of imperial caftans and the workshops that wove them document court dress.

milestones.title: Mughal court dress
milestones.blurb: Jama, patka and turban, recorded in court miniatures.
milestones.context: Under Jahangir and Shah Jahan, the court's dress is documented in miniature paintings and surviving textiles.

milestones.title: Dhaka muslin and jamdani
milestones.blurb: Ultra-fine cotton, patterned by hand in the loom.
milestones.context: Bengal muslin was prized at the Mughal court and traded widely.

milestones.title: Kosode and the widening obi
milestones.blurb: The kosode becomes the kimono, with the obi as its focus.
milestones.context: Edo-period townspeople's dress, recorded in ukiyo-e prints and surviving kosode.

milestones.title: Yuzen dyeing and kimono pattern books
milestones.blurb: Painted paste-resist dyeing and printed pattern books spread fashion.
milestones.context: Yuzen is traditionally credited to a Kyoto fan painter. The exact origin date is approximate.

milestones.title: Qing court dress
milestones.blurb: Rank shown through robes, badges and colour.
milestones.context: Court dress followed codified rules, with dragon robes and rank badges.

milestones.title: Strip-woven cloth in West Africa
milestones.blurb: Narrow woven strips sewn into prestige cloth.
milestones.context: Scholars debate the origins of regional strip-weaving traditions. Entry is placeholder for a fuller treatment.

milestones.title: Robe a la francaise and panniers
milestones.blurb: Pleated silk gowns over wide panniers.
milestones.context: Surviving gowns, portraits and plates document the court silhouette.

milestones.title: Rose Bertin, Marie Antoinette and the fashion plate
milestones.blurb: Paris milliners and printed plates set the pace.
milestones.context: Rose Bertin dressed Marie Antoinette. The Galerie des modes et costumes francais appeared 1778 to 1787.

milestones.title: Worth opens in Paris
milestones.blurb: Charles Frederick Worth founds the house that shapes haute couture.
milestones.context: The Paris house opened in 1858.

milestones.title: The 1920s silhouette
milestones.blurb: Dropped waists, shorter hems, beads and bobbed hair.
milestones.context: Illustrations, magazines, photographs and surviving dresses document the shift.

milestones.title: Paris Exposition and Art Deco
milestones.blurb: The Paris exhibition names a style that reaches dress.
milestones.context: Exposition internationale des arts decoratifs et industriels modernes, Paris, 1925.

milestones.title: Chanel's little black dress
milestones.blurb: Vogue shows a simple black dress as a uniform for all.
milestones.context: Published in American Vogue, October 1926.

milestones.title: Vionnet and the bias cut
milestones.blurb: Cloth cut on the diagonal drapes close to the body.
milestones.context: Madeleine Vionnet is central to the technique between the wars.

milestones.title: The miniskirt
milestones.blurb: Hemlines rise with youth culture.
milestones.context: Credit is shared and disputed, notably Mary Quant in London and Andre Courreges in Paris.

milestones.title: Deconstruction: Margiela and the Antwerp designers
milestones.blurb: Exposed seams, reworked garments and anonymous labels.
milestones.context: Maison Martin Margiela and Belgian designers reframe construction as subject.

milestones.title: Grunge reaches the runway
milestones.blurb: Marc Jacobs shows flannel and thrift on a luxury runway.
milestones.context: Marc Jacobs for Perry Ellis, Spring 1993.

milestones.title: Body Meets Dress, Dress Meets Body
milestones.blurb: Rei Kawakubo pads the body into new silhouettes.
milestones.context: Comme des Garcons, Spring/Summer 1997.

milestones.title: McQueen: Highland Rape to No. 13
milestones.blurb: Theatrical collections, from tartan to a robot-sprayed dress.
milestones.context: Autumn/Winter 1995 to Spring/Summer 1999.

milestones.title: Hip-hop and streetwear
milestones.blurb: Black-owned labels and big silhouettes move from the street to the mainstream.
milestones.context: Labels such as Cross Colours and Karl Kani began in 1989 and shaped the decade.
